ἢ πρὸς τὸ τοῦ μαρτυρίου στάδιον τὸ σῶμα ἐκδιδόν των, ἢ πρὸς τοὺς τῆς ἀσκήσεως
πόνους, καὶ ταύτῃ δοκούντων ἑαυτοὺς ἀπολλύναι καὶ ἀποκτεῖναι τῷ στερίσκεσθαι
τῆς βιωτικῆς ἀπολαύσεως· Ὁ ἀπολέσας τὴν ψυχὴν αὑτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ, εὑρήσει
αὐτήν. Τοῦ οὖν οὕτως ἀπολλυμένου, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ Σωτῆρος φω 377 νὴν, καὶ
εὑρίσκοντος τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ, ἡ εὐχὴ καὶ ἡ εὐλογία μεγάλη τίς ἐστιν, καὶ ταύτην
εὔξαιτο ἄν τις τῶν εὐφρονούντων ἐπελθεῖν αὑτῷ, καὶ ἐμφρόνως ἐρεῖ τό· Εὐ λογία
κτλ. ιεʹ· Ὀφθαλμὸς ἤμην τυφλῶν, ποὺς δὲ χω λῶν. Πρὸς δὲ νοῦν, τυφλὰς διανοίας
διήνοιγε, καὶ ὠφείλει τοὺς πεπηρωμένους τὴν ψυχὴν καὶ αὐτὸς αὐτῶν ἐγίνετο
ὀφθαλμός· πόδας δὲ ἐχαρίζετο τοῖς κεχωλευμένοις τὰς βάσεις τῆς ψυχῆς, καὶ τῷ
λόγῳ ἐγίνετο αὐτῶν ποὺς, καὶ ἐχειραγώγει ἑκατέρους· εἴληπται δὲ ὁ μὲν ὀφθαλμὸς
ἐπὶ τῆς νοητικῆς ὁδηγίας· ὁ δὲ ποὺς ἐπὶ τῆς ἐθικῆς. ι ʹ. Ἐγὼ ἤμην πάτερ ἀδυνάτων.
Ἐν τούτοις φωναὶ δηλοῦνται τοῦ ὠφε λοῦντος τοὺς ἀδυνάτους, τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς. ι ʹ.
∆ίκην δὲ ἣν οὐκ ᾔδειν, ἐξιχνίασα. Ὁρᾶς τὴν προστασίαν· οὐ μέχρι χρημά των, οὐδὲ
μέχρι τροφῆς καὶ ἐνδυμάτων, ἀλλὰ καὶ μέχρι κινδύνων ἀλλοτρίας προϊστάμην
μάχης. ιζʹ. Συνέτριψα δὲ μύλας ἀδίκων. Ὅρα τὴν δυσχολίαν τοῦ πράγματος· καθὰ
πόθεν, φησὶν, ἤδη καὶ προληφθὲν τὸ πρᾶγμα ἀνώρθωσα. Ἀληθῶς ὁ Χριστὸς ἐλθὼν,
τὰς μύ λας τῶν ἀντικειμένων ἐνεργειῶν συνέθλασε· τὰς μύλας τῶν λεόντων
συνέτριψεν ὁ Κύ ριος, καὶ ἐν τῷ προφήτῃ γέγραπται· Ἐκ μέ σου ὀδόντων αὐτῶν
ἅρπαγμα ἐξήρπασα. ιηʹ. Εἶπα δέ· Ἡ ἡλικία μου γηράσει, ὥσ περ στέλεχος φοίνικος.
Ὅρα δὲ μετὰ πόσον χρόνον ταῦτα λέγει, οὐχὶ καυχώμενος, οὐδὲ μεγαλοφρονῶν,
ἀλλ' ἀναγκαζόμενος εἰπεῖν τοῦ Θεοῦ τὴν πρό νοιαν, καὶ ἐπὶ τίσιν ἀπέλαυεν αὐτοῦ,
καὶ ἐν τίσιν ἐστὶ νῦν. Κεφ. Λʹ, αʹ. Νυνὶ δὲ κατεγέλασάν μου 378 ἐλάχιστοι· νῦν
νουθετοῦσί με ἐν μέρει, ὧν ἐξουδένουν τοὺς πατέρας αὐτῶν. Οὐ χρώμενος τῇ
ἐξουδενώσει, ἀλλὰ σαφῶς εἰδὼς αὐτοὺς, ὥσπερ ὁ προφήτης ἔλεγεν· Ἐξουδενοῦται
ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ πᾶς πονηρευό μενος· τοὺς γὰρ τοιούτους οὐδὲν ἡγεῖτο. βʹ, γʹ. Καί γε
ἰσχὺς χειρῶν αὐτῶν, ἱνατί μοι; ἐπ' αὐτοὺς ἀπώλετο συντέλεια. Ἐν ἐν δείᾳ καὶ λιμῷ
ἄγονος, οἱ φεύγοντες ἄνυδρον ἐχθὲς συνοχὴν καὶ ταλαιπωρίαν. Ὀλυμπιοδώρου,
Ὠριγένους. Ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ᾔτησά τινα ἐπικουρίαν, φησὶ, παρ' αὐτῶν, ἵνα διὰ τοῦτο
τοιούτοις πρὸς ἐμὲ χρήσωνται ῥήμασιν· οἵ γε πάλαι δίκην ἐχρεώστουν, πο νηροὶ
ὄντες, καὶ τρόπον τινὰ ἀπέπτη ἀπ' αὐ τῶν ἡ τιμωρία. Ἢ ὅτι θανάτου ἐπιθυμοῦντες
διὰ τὴν ἄκραν πενίαν, οὐκ ἔτυχον, καὶ οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τῆς ἐνδείας ἐσωφρονίσθησαν
γεννηταὶ γενέσθαι τοῦ καλοῦ, ἀλλ' ἔμειναν ἄγονοι, οἱ ἐχθές που καὶ πρὸ ὀλίγου, τῆς
ἐρήμου καὶ τῶν συμφορῶν ἐκπεφευγότες· ἔοικεν δὲ ὡς ἀγεννεῖς αὐτοὺς διαβάλλειν,
καὶ ἐξ ἀδόξων ὄντας χωρίων καὶ πατέρων πενήτων. Ἐπ' αὐτοὺς ἀπώλετο συντέλεια.
Ἀντὶ τοῦ, οὐδέποτέ τι χρηστὸν συνετέ λεσαν. δʹ. Οἱ περικυκλοῦντες ἄλιμα ἐπὶ
ἠχοῦντι, οἵτινες ἄλιμα ἦν αὐτῶν τὰ σῖτα. Ἄλιμα βοτάνη τις ἐστὶν, ὥς φασι, ταχὺ
πληροῦσα τὸν ἐσθίοντα. –Ἐπὶ ἠχοῦντι δὲ, τουτέστιν ἐπὶ φάραγξι καὶ πετρώδεσιν· εὔη
χοι γὰρ οἱ τοιοῦτοι τόποι, καὶ ἀντηχοῦσι τοῖς φθεγγομένοις. Ἢ καὶ ἠχοῦντα λέγει
τὸν ἀλσώδη τόπον ἐν ᾧπερ ἡ πνοὴ τῶν ἀνέμων, κινοῦσα τὴν ὕλην, ἦχον ἀποτελεῖ.
Φησὶν οὖν ὅτι περιενόστουν οὗτοι τὰς ὕλας καὶ τὰς φάραγγας καὶ τοὺς τόπους παρ'
οὓς ὕδατα ῥέοντα ἠχεῖ τε καὶ κελαρύζει, ὑπὸ τῆς ἄγαν ἐνδείας, τὰς βοτάνας
ἀνερευνώ μενοι, καὶ τὰς ῥίζας τῶν ξύλων περιξέοντες εἰς τροφὴν [λιμοῦ]
παραμυθίαν. 379 δʹ. Ἄτιμοι δὲ καὶ πεφαυλισμένοι, ἐνδεεῖς παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ. Ἑτέρα
πονηρία, τὸ καὶ ἐν πενίᾳ τοιού τους εἶναι. κδʹ. Εἰ γὰρ ὄφελον δυναίμην ἐμαυτὸν χει
ρώσασθαι. Ὁρᾷς ὅτι τὸ εἰ δυναίμην, οὐ διὰ ἀσθέ νειαν λέγει, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸ
κεκωλῦσθαι. κηʹ. Ἕστηκα δὲ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ κεκραγώς. ∆ιὰ τὴν ὑπερβολὴν τῶν δεινῶν,
οὐδὲ πλῆ θος συνόδου αἰσχυνόμενος. κθʹ. Ἀδελφὸς γέγονα Σειρήνων, ἑταῖρος δὲ
στρουθῶν. Εἰς τὴν ὀρνίθων θηριωδίαν ἐξέπεσα, φη σίν· ἠγνόησα τὴν φύσιν τὴν
οἰκείαν, οὐδὲν ἐκείνων ἀμείνων διάκειμαι. Κεφ. ΛΑʹ, ʹ, ζʹ. Ἕσταμαι γὰρ ἐν ζυγῷ
δικαίῳ, οἶδε δὲ ὁ Κύριος τὴν ἀκακίαν μου, εἰ ἐξέκλινεν ὁ ποῦς μου ἐκ τῆς ὁδοῦ ...
Βαβαὶ τῆς ἀκριβείας! οὐκ ἔχοι τις εἰ πεῖν, ὅτι τῷ πλούτῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς τοῖς
ἔμπροσθεν εἰς ῥᾳθυμίαν καὶ διάχυσιν ἀπο χρησάμενος τοιαύτην τίνω δίκην, καὶ με
ταβέβλημαι, τοῦ Θεοῦ κατάλληλόν μοι φάρ μακον ἐπιθέντος. Τὸν μὲν γὰρ φιλόγελω
καὶ φιλοπταίσμονα καὶ τρυφῇ προσεσχηκότα, εἰκότως ἀντιθεὶς, τὴν ἐναντίαν
pass_a_gloss: ...or toward the stadium of martyrdom giving over the body, or toward the labours of ascesis, and in this way seeming to destroy and kill themselves by being deprived of life's enjoyment: he who lost his soul for my sake will find it. Of the one thus perishing, according to the Saviour's voice, and finding his soul, the prayer and the blessing is something great, and this one of the sensible would pray to come upon himself, and sensibly he will say: Blessing etc. Verse 15. I was an eye of the blind, a foot of the lame. As to mind, he opened blind thoughts, and helped those maimed in soul and himself became their eye; and he granted feet to those lamed in the steps of the soul, and by word became their foot, and led each by hand; the eye is taken of noetic guidance, the foot of ethical. Verse 16. I was father of the powerless. In these, voices are shown of one helping the powerless, the weak. Verse 16. Justice which I did not know I tracked out. You see the patronage: not as far as money, nor as far as food and clothing, but even as far as dangers I stood before another's battle. Verse 17. I crushed the millstones (molars) of the unjust. See the difficulty of the matter; whence (?) he says, even the matter already seized beforehand I set upright. Truly Christ having come crushed the molars of the opposing energies; the molars of the lions the Lord crushed, and in the prophet it is written: from the middle of their teeth I snatched a seizure. Verse 18. I said: my age will grow old, like a stem of a palm. See after how much time he says these, not boasting, nor being proud, but being compelled to say the providence of God, and in what he enjoyed it, and in what he is now. Chapter 30, verse 1. Now the least mocked me; now they admonish me in turn, whose fathers I set at nought. Not using the setting at nought, but clearly knowing them, as the prophet said: every one doing evil is set at nought before him; for he considered such as nothing. Verses 2, 3. Even the strength of their hands, why to me? Upon them perished completion. In lack and famine barren, those fleeing waterless yesterday constraint and misery. Of Olympiodorus, of Origen. But I did not even ask some help, he says, from them, so that because of this they use such words toward me; they who long owed justice, being wicked, and in a way the punishment flew off from them. Or that desiring death because of extreme poverty they did not obtain, and not even by lack were they brought to sense to become begetters of the good, but remained barren, those yesterday somewhere and a little before having fled from the desert and the misfortunes; he seems to slander them as ignoble, and from inglorious places and poor fathers. Upon them perished completion: instead of, they never accomplished anything useful. Verse 4. Those circling mallows on an echoing, whose mallows were their food. Mallow is a certain herb, as they say, quickly filling the eater. On echoing, that is on ravines and rocky places; for such places are resonant and echo back to those speaking. Or he calls echoing the wooded place in which the breath of winds, moving the timber, produces echo. He says then that these roamed the woods and ravines and places by which flowing waters sound and babble, by excessive need searching the herbs, and scraping around the roots of trees for food, consolation (of hunger). Verse 4. Dishonoured and made worthless, lacking every good. Another wickedness, to be such even in poverty. Verse 24. For would that I could subdue myself. You see that the 'if I could' he says not through weakness but through being hindered. Verse 28. I have stood in assembly having cried. Through the excess of the terrible things, not ashamed even of the crowd of the gathering. Verse 29. Brother I have become of sirens, companion of ostriches. Into the beastliness of birds I fell, he says; I was ignorant of my own nature, I am disposed nothing better than those. Chapter 31, verses 6, 7. For I stand in a just yoke (balance), and the Lord knows my innocence, if my foot turned aside from the way... Wow, the exactness! one could not say that having misused the wealth and the goods before into idleness and dissipation I pay such a penalty, and have been changed, God having laid on me a fitting medicine. For the laughter-lover and play-lover (φιλοπταίσμονα, read φιλοπαίγμονα?) and attached to luxury, fittingly setting against, the opposite...
pass_b_english: … or who give the body over to the stadium of martyrdom, or to the labours of the ascetic life, and in this way seem to destroy and kill themselves by being deprived of the enjoyments of life: “He who loses his life for my sake will find it” (Matthew 10:39). For one who perishes in this way, according to the Saviour's word, and finds his life, the prayer and the blessing is a great thing. Anyone of sound mind would pray that it might come upon him, and would wisely say: “The blessing,” and so on (Job 29:13).

“I was an eye to the blind, and a foot to the lame” (Job 29:15). As to the mind, he opened blind understandings and helped those maimed in soul, and he himself became their eye. To those lamed in the steps of the soul he gave feet; by his word he became their foot and led both by the hand. The eye stands for guidance of the understanding, the foot for guidance of conduct.

“I was a father of the powerless” (Job 29:16). These words show the voice of one who helps the powerless, the weak. “And a cause that I did not know, I searched out” (Job 29:16). You see his protection: it did not stop at money, nor at food and clothing; I stood forward even to the point of danger in another man's fight.

“And I broke the molars of the unjust” (Job 29:17). See how hard the thing was: he says that he set the matter right even when it had already been seized. Truly Christ, when he came, crushed the molars of the opposing powers. “The Lord has broken the molars of the lions” (Psalm 58:6), and it is written in the prophet: “From the midst of their teeth I snatched the prey” (Job 29:17).

“And I said: My age will grow old like the stem of a palm” (Job 29:18). See after how long a time he says this: not boasting or thinking great things of himself, but compelled to speak of God's providence, of the things in which he enjoyed it and of where he stands now.

“But now the least have laughed at me; now they admonish me in their turn, whose fathers I set at nought” (Job 30:1). Not that he made a practice of contempt, but that he knew them clearly, as the prophet said: “Every evildoer is set at nought before him” (Psalm 15:4). For he counted such people as nothing.
“And the strength of their hands, what is it to me? Over them the full end has perished. In want and famine he is barren, those who yesterday fled from waterless distress and misery” (Job 30:2-3).

From Olympiodorus and Origen: I did not even ask them for any help, he says, that they should use such words against me on that account. They had long owed a penalty, being wicked, and in a way the punishment flew away from them. Or else: they longed for death because of their extreme poverty and did not obtain it, and not even their want brought them to their senses so as to become begetters of good; they remained barren, those who only yesterday, a little while ago, had escaped from the desert and their misfortunes. He seems to disparage them as low-born, from obscure villages and poor fathers. “Over them the full end has perished”: that is, they never brought anything good to completion.

“Those who go round the mallows on an echoing place, whose food was mallows” (Job 30:4). Mallow is a plant, they say, that quickly fills the one who eats it. “On an echoing place”: that is, on ravines and rocky ground, for such places ring and give back the voices of those who speak. Or he calls echoing the wooded place where the breath of the winds stirs the trees and makes a sound. So he says that these men roamed the woods and the ravines and the places where running waters sound and babble; in their great want they searched out plants and scraped the roots of trees for food, as some comfort in their hunger.
“Dishonoured and despised, in want of every good thing” (Job 30:4). It is another wickedness to be like this even in poverty.
“For would that I could lay hands on myself” (Job 30:24). You see that he says “if I could” not because of weakness but because he was forbidden.
“And I have stood in the assembly crying out” (Job 30:28). Because of the excess of his sufferings he is not ashamed even of the crowd of the gathering.

“I have become a brother of sirens and a companion of ostriches” (Job 30:29). I have fallen, he says, into the wildness of the birds; I have forgotten my own nature, and I am in no better state than they.

“For I have stood in a just balance, and the Lord knows my innocence, if my foot has turned aside from the way …” (Job 31:6-7). What exactness! No one could say that I misused my former wealth and goods for idleness and dissipation and so pay this penalty and have been changed, God having laid on me a fitting medicine. For to the one who loves laughter and play and is given to luxury he fittingly sets the opposite …
